scope_note: Exhibits transcribe the field/value pairs a candidate reads on the controller, grouped by tab, rather than drawing an invented web page in ASCII.

items.stem: Refer to the exhibit. Why can no client see or join this WLAN?

exhibit.content:
WLC GUI  -  WLANs > Edit > CORP-WIFI

Tab: General
    Profile Name                  CORP-WIFI
    SSID                          CORP-WIFI
    Status                        Disabled
    Radio Policy                  All
    Interface/Interface Group     vlan10-corp
    Broadcast SSID                Enabled

Tab: Security > Layer 2
    Layer 2 Security              WPA+WPA2
    WPA2 Policy                   Enabled
    WPA2 Encryption               AES
    Authentication Key Mgmt       PSK

The access points are joined and healthy, VLAN 10 is reachable, and the
pre-shared key has been distributed. No client can see or join CORP-WIFI.

options.text: Broadcast SSID is enabled, which hides the network from ordinary clients.
The WLAN's Status is Disabled, so it is never advertised.
The Radio Policy of All prevents the WLAN binding to any single band.
WPA2 with PSK cannot be used together with an interface group.

items.explanation: A WLAN is only pushed to the access points once its Status is Enabled, so with it disabled the SSID is never advertised no matter how complete the rest of the configuration is. Option A reverses the meaning of Broadcast SSID, which when enabled makes the network visible rather than hiding it. Option C misreads Radio Policy, where All means both bands carry the WLAN rather than none. Option D invents a conflict; WPA2 with a pre-shared key on a mapped interface is an ordinary combination.

items.stem: Refer to the exhibit. Which two statements describe what a guest experiences on this WLAN? (Choose two.)

exhibit.content:
WLC GUI  -  WLANs > Edit > GUEST-WIFI

Tab: General
    Profile Name                  GUEST-WIFI
    SSID                          GUEST-WIFI
    Status                        Enabled
    Interface/Interface Group     vlan90-guest

Tab: Security > Layer 2
    Layer 2 Security              None

Tab: Security > Layer 3
    Layer 3 Security              Web Policy
    Web Policy                    Authentication

options.text: They are prompted for a pre-shared key when they associate.
They cannot associate at all until a Layer 2 security method is set.
They associate with no key, and their traffic crosses the air unencrypted.
A browser is intercepted and credentials are demanded before access is granted.
Their traffic becomes encrypted once web authentication succeeds.

items.explanation: Layer 2 Security reads None, so association needs no key and nothing protects the radio link, while the Layer 3 Web Policy intercepts the browser and demands credentials before granting access. Option A describes a pre-shared key the configuration does not set. Option B is contradicted by this being an ordinary working guest arrangement. Option E is the tempting error: web authentication decides who may pass traffic and never turns on link-layer encryption, so guest traffic stays readable throughout.

items.stem: Refer to the exhibit. Which change on the controller addresses the reported audio problem?

exhibit.content:
WLC GUI  -  WLANs > Edit > VOICE-WIFI

Tab: General
    Profile Name                  VOICE-WIFI
    SSID                          VOICE-WIFI
    Status                        Enabled
    Interface/Interface Group     vlan20-voice

Tab: QoS
    Quality of Service (QoS)      Silver (best effort)
    Application Visibility        Disabled
    WMM Policy                    Allowed

Handsets on this WLAN report choppy audio whenever the office data
network is busy. Wired QoS is already trusting and prioritising the
voice VLAN correctly end to end.

options.text: Disable the WMM Policy, so voice frames are no longer queued behind data.
Enable Application Visibility so the controller can identify the voice stream.
Set Quality of Service on this WLAN to Platinum, the profile intended for voice.
Move the WLAN to the data interface so it shares the wired queue already trusted.

items.explanation: The wired path is already prioritising voice, so the gap is over the air: this WLAN sits on Silver, the best-effort profile, and voice needs Platinum, which is the profile the controller reserves for it. Option A removes the very mechanism that gives voice frames preferential radio access. Option B adds visibility and reporting without changing how frames are queued. Option D moves voice onto the data network, which would undo the separation that makes the wired prioritisation work.

items.stem: Refer to the exhibit. What does the Maximum Allowed Clients value of 0 mean for this WLAN?

exhibit.content:
WLC GUI  -  WLANs > Edit > CORP-WIFI

Tab: Advanced
    Enable Session Timeout        1800 seconds
    Client Exclusion              Enabled, 60 seconds
    Maximum Allowed Clients       0
    Aironet IE                    Enabled
    P2P Blocking Action           Disabled
    Client Load Balancing         Disabled

options.text: No limit is applied; clients are capped by hardware alone.
The WLAN is closed to clients until an administrator raises the figure.
Clients are admitted one at a time as earlier sessions time out.
The value is ignored while Client Exclusion remains enabled.

items.explanation: On this page zero is the value meaning unlimited rather than none, so the WLAN accepts clients up to whatever the access points and controller can carry. Option B reads zero literally, which would silently take a working WLAN out of service and is the reason the convention is worth knowing. Option C invents a queueing behaviour tied to the session timeout above it. Option D links the field to Client Exclusion, which governs how long a misbehaving client is locked out rather than how many may join.
